Zero to Report

Two coding agents took one question — how do we stop spending GPU on video where nothing moves? — from zero setup to two finished reports, for a GPU bill under ten dollars.

The gate must cost less than it saves, never stop real motion, and hold on scenes it was not tuned on.

Client environment setup

models

Self-hosted GLM-5.2 for code

  • The agent cannot call any external API — everything runs inside the client's network.
  • GLM-5.2 is strong at code, has no vision, and carries a generous internal quota.
models

Vision routed to Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B

  • opencode.json + omo route image tasks to self-hosted Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B.
  • Result: the agent can check its own screenshots, plots, and extracted frames.
skills

multimodal-inspection skill

  • Replaces the vague default look_at — one unclear instruction for all image tasks.
  • Hooks normalize every input: video and HTML pages are converted to static images before the vision model sees them.
skills

remote-dev skill

  • Coding workspace has no GPU access; the cluster is reachable only via JupyterLab.
  • The skill syncs code to the cluster, runs the experiment there, pulls results back — agents follow it automatically.

The morning the letters began arriving, Tomas counted eleven of them before breakfast, each one shoved through the letter slot with a violence the postman surely did not intend. His aunt gathered them up with a soup ladle — she refused to touch them with her bare hands — and burned them in the kitchen sink, one at a time, pressing each under the water with the ladle until the ink bled loose and the paper fell apart into a grey pulp that swirled down the drain. Nobody spoke at the table. His cousin chewed with his mouth open and watched the sink the way a dog watches a door it has been beaten behind.

The letters kept coming. On Tuesday one was tucked inside a loaf of bread; on Wednesday another was folded into the gas bill; on Thursday a third was taped beneath the milk bottles, so that by the end of the week the whole street knew something strange was happening at number nine and had begun to take sides. The widow at number eleven said it was marketing. The twins at fourteen said it was a secret admirer. Old Baruzi from the corner shop, who had survived three governments and two marriages, said it was neither, bought Tomas a chocolate, and did not explain.

Tomas had managed to read exactly one letter, the fourth, for perhaps six seconds, before his aunt caught him holding it and made him watch it die in the sink. He had seen only the first line — Mr T. Vale, third door past the boiler, we are pleased to inform you — and then the ink went soft, and the words ran like footprints in rain, and the ladle came down.

What he felt was not curiosity, exactly. It was the feeling of standing in a large station and hearing, underneath the announcements and the brakes and the crowd, a second clock running slightly out of time with the first. Once heard, it could not be unheard. He began to notice other things: that the cat waited for him at the corner every afternoon and walked him home like a guard; that his aunt's thermometer, shaken down and boiled and shaken down again, still read one degree too warm whenever he held it; that the back step of the house, which had been loose for eleven years, had gone suddenly, insolently firm.

On Sunday the knocking started. Three slow knocks at the front door at exactly noon, then nothing; three more at one o'clock; three more at two. His aunt turned the television up. His cousin laughed, then stopped laughing, because at three o'clock the three knocks came not from the front door but from inside the cupboard where the mops lived — politely, at knee height, as though asking permission.

Tomas opened the cupboard himself. He did not decide to; his hands decided, and he went along the way one goes along with a sneeze. Inside there were mops, a dented pail, a box of Christmas candles, and an envelope lying flat on top of the paint tin, bone-dry, though the roof had leaked onto that tin every winter since before he was born. The envelope was addressed in green-black ink, in a hand so certain it looked printed: Mr T. Vale, third door past the boiler. To be opened by the addressee only, and preferably before Tuesday.

His aunt found him like that, envelope in hand, cat at his ankle, and for a moment nobody moved, and the house held its breath along with them. Then she sat down on the stairs — really sat, the ladle still in her hand — and looked suddenly, horribly tired, and older than any photograph of her, and a little afraid.

"It was never going to miss you, was it," she said. It was not a question. "Eleven years I kept the papers away. Eleven years I kept you off the lists, out of the photographs, away from the fairs and the clinics and the census. I burned the cradle. I told them you were sick. I told them you were simple. I told them you were dead, Tomas, and I buried a jar in the churchyard with your name on it to make it stick."

"What is it?" Tomas asked, though the second clock in his ears was already loud now, already drowning out the refrigerator's hum.

"They will say it's a school," his aunt said, wiping her palms on her apron, once, twice, leaving grey smears where the ink had been. "That is the word they use. School. As if it were only lessons." She looked at the envelope the way you look at weather coming in off the sea. "Eleven years," she said again, and got up, and put the kettle on, because in her country grief and fear were both things you made tea through.

"Tuesday," said the envelope, in its certain hand. And outside, up the street, unhurried, keeping perfect time with a clock that did not exist, the knocking began again — three of them — from the letter slot of a house that had, until this week, contained no magic at all.

  • The T4 has both silicons the question needs
  • CUDA cores + NvOFA engine on one card — like production's RTX PRO 6000
  • Preflight on every new host
  • driver consistency check + gst-launch nvof smoke test
  • a failed host is deleted and replaced, not debugged
  • Local folder bind-mounted into the instance
  • code and results stay on the Mac, nothing lost at stop
  • Scripts written and static-tested on the Mac
  • instance starts only when an experiment is ready
  • stop is async — scripts poll until STOPPED
  • Idle GPU time ran installs
  • the 11-min CUDA-OpenCV build ran while waiting
  • Every launch needed a manual fix — so the fix went into the image
  • Brev's container provisioning does not survive a reboot: every start resurrected a bare container with no sshd and wedged UNHEALTHY — about 10 min of manual container repair per launch
  • the sshd bootstrap is baked into a derived image (deepstream8-ready) — launches are zero-touch, ready in ~1 min

Reports cost $0 — agents ran on plan quotas, vision ran locally. Total GPU bill: under $10 across 2–3 experiments.

Keep theory exploration out of the agent harness

Reading papers, deriving the score shape, comparing options — exploration consumes context, and the harness window is finite. The human explores offline and hands agents conclusions.

— derivations
— option comparisons
— dead ends

none of this text enters the harness
→

— use of different silicon: dedicated OFA engine vs CUDA-core occupancy
— different strategies to capture small signals:
   · aggregation
   · reshaping
→
3 · execute — agents — scripts
— benchmarks
— plots
— video overlays
— reports

measurement, not deliberation

4 · conclusion — what the agent receives one line it can execute against:
— NvOFA
— cells ≥ 0.5 px

One self-contained HTML report

Every spike ends in a single HTML file: source code and all conclusions, fully enclosed — no server, no external files, opens from file:// anywhere.

  • A fully enclosed HTML report contains source code and all conclusions
  • the code that ran sits next to the results it produced — every number traceable
  • plots, video results and the tuning controls are embedded in the same file
  • Used for proper spike closure and DDR
  • one artifact to review, archive and hand over when the spike closes
  • Guides code productionization
  • the working source inside the report is the reference for the production port
  • the two reports shipped with this deck are built exactly this way

Algorithm comparison

median compute — ms per frame
MOG211.5
Farnebäck6.5
CPU diff6.2
NvOFA0.9
GPU diff0.4
mean SM busy % — 1 Hz nvidia-smi
MOG20.0
Farnebäck35.6
CPU diff0.0
NvOFA9.9
GPU diff62.8
  • Flow measures movement; absdiff measures brightness
  • exposure shifts, headlights and shadows change pixel intensity everywhere — absdiff spikes, flow's displacement stays quiet
  • Vibration is separable in a flow field
  • shake moves all pixels with one shared vector — visible as global motion, removable as background
  • pixel differences cannot tell shake from a mover
  • The gate runs on NvOFA
  • 0.91 ms compute at 9.9% SM busy — leaves the CUDA cores to detection + tracking
  • GPU absdiff is faster (0.86 ms e2e)
  • but occupies 62.8% of the CUDA cores detection + tracking need
  • Move detection to specialized hardware
  • the OFA engine handles flow; frees general CUDA cores for downstream tasks — object detection + tracking

NvOF optimization

1 · aggregation — keep small movers visible — far mover moves few pixels: the frame-mean pools it into the static background (diluted 33× → 9×)
— some pooling is still needed for a stable score

the recipe:
— mean-pools inside 880 cells, flags cells over 0.5 px
— score = count of active cells — pooled for stability, never diluted by frame size
→
2 · reshaping — one line for both mover sizes — small- and large-mover frames score magnitudes apart: one cut fits one and misses the other
— log compresses the span (120× → 27×)
— pulls small-mover scores up toward large-mover ones

one threshold line becomes drawable
→
3 · threshold — adapt, then hold — the cut must fit each video's distribution
— fixed is simple; Otsu finds the cut automatically (bi-modal clustering) but needs score history — impractical for streaming
— one hard line + fluctuating score = fragmented motion
— hysteresis (T_hi 0.37 / T_lo 0.31 / d 3) holds the state d frames before flipping
  • A hard line fragments as the score fluctuates
  • every flip swaps cameras in/out of the nvstreammux batch
  • incurs kernel-launch latency
  • hysteresis cut motion fragmentation, e.g.
  • 12 → 5 segments (carpark·day)
  • 7 → 5 (street·night)
  • Same recipe on both clips, no hand labels
  • Otsu cut 0.17 / 0.322
  • confidence η 0.928 / 0.739
  • judged by η, throttled duty, bootstrap stability, and 4-lane agreement

Takeaways

  • Spike with agents, rent GPU only when ready
  • develop locally, start/stop per experiment
  • bill stayed under $10
  • Keep theory exploration out of the agent harness
  • agents get conclusions, not the exploration
  • context is finite
  • Local VLM for bulk vision checks
  • API vision bills per image; local model answers "is this chart rendered?" for free
  • A fully enclosed HTML report contains source code and all conclusions
  • used for proper spike closure and DDR
  • guides code productionization
  • Fully use the coding agent for visualization
  • extensive plots and overlays are cheap to generate, and always help decision making
  • One e2e run and report first, then iterate
  • we don't know what we don't know
  • the full pass reveals which questions matter next
